title: Low-Balance Alert Election on Automatic Replenishment — Paystride Instant Pay Disbursement Service Desk Tool Reference
content:
## The alert level and the replenishment floor

This rule settles the replenishment floor, the lowest alert level Paystride accepts on a Paystride Instant Pay Disbursement Service with automatic replenishment on. The employer may change its funding method, auto replenishment or alert level at any time while the service is not closed, and auto replenishment can be turned on only on tiers that allow automatic replenishment; on a service with automatic replenishment on, an alert level is recorded only at or above the replenishment floor.

Because the alert level of a service with automatic replenishment decides when Paystride debits the employer's bank account, setting it is the employer's own election: the desk works out the replenishment floor, the authorized employer contact confirms it in person, and that confirmation records the floor as the alert level on file while automatic replenishment stays on.

## Recording the election

The alert level is recorded with `confirm_alert_level_1c610295`, a tool the customer themselves runs: the agent unlocks it and hands it over, and the employer's authorized contact runs it in person.

**Capability.** The employer's authorized contact confirms, in person, the low-balance alert level of the employer's Instant Pay Disbursement service, the balance below which automatic replenishment debits are pulled from the employer's bank account. One call records the confirmed amount as the service's alert level on file and leaves the funding method and the automatic replenishment setting as they are; the employer sees the new alert level on its service at once.

### Parameters

- `disburse_service_id` — the reference number of the employer's Instant Pay Disbursement service, as read to the employer by the desk from the service record (identifier).
- `low_balance_alert_usd` — the alert level the employer confirms, in US dollars as a positive number with exactly 2 decimal places; a value with more decimals is rounded half up to the cent before it is recorded.

### Return

- A one-line confirmation naming the service reference (text), the previous alert level (US dollars, two decimals) and the alert level now on file (US dollars, two decimals). The new alert level being reported means the election was recorded.
- A message beginning "Not recorded" means the amount was not greater than zero and nothing changed.

### Contract illustration (hypothetical values)

A `low_balance_alert_usd` of 1234.567 is recorded as 1234.57, and the reply shows the level previously on file beside it; a `low_balance_alert_usd` of 0 returns a message beginning "Not recorded".
